title: Evaluation sampler capture: quant onboarding + microbatch probes (Oct 19–21 2027)
content:
Purpose / context:
Quick working notes from this week's applied-ml standups and ad-hoc sessions. Focus: how to pick evaluation subsets ("samplers") that reveal quality regressions when we quantize or change microbatching/KV caching behaviors during model onboarding. Trying to capture heuristics so solutions-engineering can reproduce and so we can instrument the console evals pipeline.

High-level takeaway:
- Small biased samplers hide regressions. Need multi-strategy sampler that mixes tail-case prompts, slot-filling templates, and noisy real-traffic snippets.
- Microbatch size changes (1 -> 8) changed latency profile but also introduced subtle tokenization alignment differences for a couple of f2f Spanish prompts — likely due to model tokenization boundary + caching edge.
- 4-bit quant variant shows 0.9–1.6% BLEU-like drop on slot-fill tests but up to 7% hallucination increase on open-ended prompts; mitigations: targeted per-layer quant thresholds and reranking on top-k.

This week's experiments (runs):
- run: eval-sampler-A (2027-10-19) — stratified sampler = {10% tail-case, 40% templates, 50% traffic-clip}. Model: base-7B-fp16 -> q4_kv_prefetch. Microbatch: 1. KV cache policy: default.
- run: eval-sampler-B (2027-10-20) — same dataset, microbatch 8, kv_prefetch on, compare streaming vs buffered.
- run: eval-sampler-C (2027-10-20) — q4 with per-layer clamp on attention matrices (layers 0-4 tighter scaling).
- run: eval-sampler-D (2027-10-21) — top-k rerank (k=3) applied to q4 output for open-ended tests only.

Quick numeric summary (approx):
- templates (slot-fill) accuracy: fp16 94.8% | q4 93.1% | q4+rerank 93.9%
- tail-case BLEU-ish: fp16 71.2 | q4 67.1 | q4+per-layer 68.6
- hallucination rate (open-ended): fp16 4.6% | q4 11.3% | q4+rerank 6.9%
- median latency (per-token, microbatch=1): fp16 18ms | q4 12ms | q4 microbatch=8 8ms
- P95 latency moved +7ms in microbatch=8 for streaming mode due to flush alignment on partial batches

Observations / notes:
- Sampling matters: when we used just traffic clips most regressions disappeared; the templates and tail-case buckets were necessary to surface the quant-induced hallucinations.
- Reranking helps for open-ended hallucinations but costs ~1.6x tokens due to top-k scoring; consider serving-time signal (only enable rerank if open-ended flag set).
- Microbatching benefits throughput but exposes behavior differences tied to tokenizer boundary handling when KV cache gets prefilled across requests. Evan to open quick repro in runtimes (PR reference above).
- Per-layer quant thresholds: early attention layers are sensitive; tightening clamp for 0-3 reduced the worst hallucinations but made some syntactic artifacts in French examples. We need per-lingual validation slices.

Standup capture (2027-10-21):
- Nina: summary of runs + immediate ask: add traffic-label metadata to eval pipeline so we can slice by prompt-type ("slot", "tail", "open", "code").
- Evan: will prototype a small adapter in runtimes that enforces deterministic token flush for streaming + microbatch (PR #1284).
- Marta: to add Spanish/French tokenization sanity tests in onboarding harness; will add to unit test suite.
- Samir: prepare a cost estimate for rerank-on-demand (expected +12–18% token cost for open-ended heavy routes).

Open questions / discussion items:
- What threshold of hallucination increase is acceptable per customer tier? (dev vs enterprise SLA). Suggest: <2% for enterprise critical routes. Need product input.
- Should reranking be a model variant (q4-rerank) or an opt-in runtime hook? Tradeoff: variant increases model catalog complexity; runtime hook increases latency variability.
- Is microbatch=8 safe for low-latency endpoints? We saw P95 tail regress in streaming mode. Can we do adaptive microbatching per-route?

Action items (owner - ETA):
- Add traffic-labels to eval ingestion pipeline (Nina - 2027-10-25)
- Minimal repro for tokenizer+kv issue and link to runtimes PR (Evan - 2027-10-22) -> PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtimes/pull/1284
- Add French/Spanish tokenization tests to onboarding harness (Marta - 2027-10-26)
- Cost model for rerank-on-demand and a console toggle proposal (Samir - 2027-10-28)
- Small A/B in staging for q4+per-layer clamp vs q4 baseline (Nina + Applied ML infra - 2027-11-02)

Notes to self / working hypotheses:
- Hypothesis 1: hallucination spikes are correlated with tail-case grammatical constructs that result in longer attention keys; look at attention norm distributions.
- Hypothesis 2: microbatch flush timing + tokenizer alignment causes KV cache to present slightly different context order at boundaries; small but amplifies in certain languages.

Quick command snippets used (for reproducibility):
- run eval locally: python experiments/eval_pipeline.py --sampler stratified --seed 42 --model base-7B-fp16 --variant q4 --microbatch 1 --out runs/eval-A
- run rerank: python experiments/rerank.py --input runs/eval-C --k 3 --model scorer-small

References & links:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtimes/pull/1284
- Jira: AI-4529 (quant onboarding checklist), AI-4571 (sampling infra work)

Random notes (informal):
- Heard from Solutions that a customer reported odd truncation on Spanish biographies — might be related to tokenizer boundary thing we're seeing. Pinged SE (Slack thread: #solutions-onboarding).
- Consider adding a small suite of "stress prompts" (100 prompts) that are explicitly designed to surface q4 regressions; can be used as part of per-release gate.

If you're skimming: the main short-term priorities are (1) traffic-labels in eval ingestion, (2) runtimes repro for flush/tokenizer, (3) cost calc + console toggle for rerank. Everything else is lower priority.

End of capture.
